# **_Economic Background_** - In the US the residential construction market remains in dire straits despite the unexpected 22% month-on-month increase in housing starts in February. On a year-on-year basis starts fell by 47% and permits declined by 44%. However, even with the dramatically slower pace of construction stocks of new homes remain at a record high, equivalent to 13 months of supply. A further indication of the downturn comes from the US durable capital goods data which fell by 5.4% in January, the fifth monthly decline in the last six months. - With 35-40% of Chinese GDP accounted for by exports, the recessions in many of the world’s mature economies have resulted in large scale factory closures in China’s coastal manufacturing hubs and resulted in over 20M migrant workers being made unemployed and forced to return to their rural homes. In January exports posted a year-on-year decline of 17.5% and in February the decline was 25.7%. Furthermore, job losses and China’s poor social safety net for the unemployed has prompted consumers to cut spending and increase savings. During each the final six months of 2008 growth in Chinese retail sales averaged 21.9% year on year. However, for the first two months of 2009 this growth rate slumped to 15.2%. - The South Korean economy has been dealt a severe blow by the collapse in demand from its major trading partners. As a result, industrial production fell 19% year on year in December and 25% in January. Last year, car production declined by 7.3% to 3.4M units and sales fell 2.8% to 959 thousand units. However, the relatively modest annual declines mask the rapid deterioration of the automotive sector in the final two months of 2008 and January this year. In year-on-year terms South Korean car production fell by 20% in November, 26% in December and by 48% in January this year. - Global demand is collapsing at an even faster rate than previously forecast and our estimate of a contraction of 1.9% in global IP this year now appears to be optimistic. We will publish updated forecasts in the April report. INDUSTRIAL PRODUCTION

- US IP fell by 11.2% year on year in February, down 1.4% from the previous month. - Japanese IP (seasonally adjusted) in February declined by 37.7% year on year, a fall of 9.5% from January. - South Korean IP (seasonally adjusted) fell by 25.6% in January compared with January 2008. - January IP (seasonally adjusted) in the euro zone and EU 27 fell by 17.3% and by 16.3% year on year respectively. IP in France, Germany, Italy, Spain and the UK fell by 14%, 19.4%, 16.7%, 19.1% and 11.1% year on year respectively. - The year-on-year rate of growth of Chinese IP was 3.8% in the first two months of 2009. - In January, industrial output in Brazil, Russia and India fell by 17.2%, 16% and 0.5% year on year respectively. - US production of light vehicles fell by 54.9% in February year on year. Output of cars and light trucks declined annually by 55.5% and by 54.6% respectively. - In Japan car production fell by 41.2% year on year in January to 495k units and total vehicle production declined by 41%. - According to the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers, during the period January-February production of passenger vehicles rose by 23% year on year and output of cars increased by 25.4% annually. - Korean vehicle production in January declined by 47.7% year on year: car output fell by 48.1% and commercial vehicle production declined by 43.8%. - US private housing starts rose by 22.2% in February from January, a decline of 47.3% year on year. - In January Japanese housing starts fell by 14% compared with December and were down 18.7% from January 2008. - Korean housing permits, on a floor area basis, slumped by 63.3% year on year in January. - In December German housing permits declined by 9.0% year on year to 14,278. _March 2009_ _Page 2_ _Economic Outlook_ _Brook Hunt_ ### **CONSUMERS** REAL RETAIL SALES

- Advance estimates of nominal US retail sales for February, on a seasonally adjusted basis, fell by 8.6% year on year and declined 0.1% from January. US real retail sales declined by 10.2% year on year in January, an increase of 1.5% from the previous month. - In January the volume of retail sales in the euro zone rose by 0.1% from December but fell 2.2% from a year ago. - Japanese real retail sales rose by 0.1% year on year in January, up by 1.5% from December. - According to the National Bureau of Statistics, Chinese nominal retail sales rose by 18.5% year on year in January and by 11.6% in February. - In the US the number of unemployed persons and the unemployment rate rose to 12.5 million and 8.1% respectively in February. - The euro zone unemployment rate in January rose to 8.2%. The rate in France increased to 8.3% and in Germany to 7.3%. - The Japanese unemployment rate rose to 4.4% in February, up from 4.1% in January. ### **INVESTMENT** CAPACITY UTILIZATION - MANUFACTURING

The February rate for manufacturing fell to 67.4% from 67.9% the previous month. - Eurostat’s Q1 2009 estimate of EU capacity utilization fell to 74.9% from 81% in Q4. - The Japanese index of capacity utilization in January fell by 12.9% from December to 68 (2005=100), down by 34.9% from a year ago. - Korean capacity utilization rose to 66.7% in February from 61.4% in January - US new orders for manufactured durable goods fell by 4.5% month on month in January to $164.96Bn (seasonally adjusted), a decline of 22.8% year on year. - Japanese machinery orders (excluding ships and orders by power utilities) declined by 39.6% year on year in January to ¥718Bn - The seasonally-adjusted index of German durable goods orders in January fell by 7.0% from December and by 20.5% year on year. _March 2009_ _Page 3_ _Economic Outlook_ _Brook Hunt_ ### **KEY INDICATORS** USGS LEADING INDEX OF PRIMARY METALS

- The USGS primary metals leading index fell by 18.1% year on year to 122.8 in February 2009, a decline of 2.9% compared with the January figure of 126.5. - The US Institute of Supply Management’s PMI for manufacturing industries increased slightly to 35.8 in February from 35.6 points in January. - The Bank of Japan’s (BoJ) Tankan diffusion index of business conditions for all industries was -24 in Q4 2008 and is forecast to fall to -38 in Q1 2009. The index for manufacturing was -25 in Q4 2008 and the BoJ forecasts that it will fall to -44 in Q1 2009. - The European Commission’s index of euro zone industrial confidence fell again in February to record a historical low of –39.2. - The US Conference Board’s Consumer Confidence Index in February fell 12.4 points to 25, an all-time low. - The European Commission’s index of euro zone consumer confidence in March fell to –33.7, its lowest level since January 1985. - The Japanese consumer confidence index rose by 1.1% in February from January, a decline of 29% from a year ago. - The differential between the three-year US Government Bond and the US Treasury Bill in February was an estimated 1.07. The estimated average T-Bill stood at 0.3% in February.
